conversation.content: can you see my code code routines from here
Hah! My noble friend, let Squeers cast his good eye about and see what mischief the boys 'ave left lyin' in the schoolroom.

Aye, my dear and faithful friend, Squeers can see plain as a pikestaff! 'Tis no proper code-shop here, mind — only a great heap o' Flowstone scribblin's, near two hundred Markdown notes, all stacked up like the bony lads at Dotheboys Hall come breakfast time. Project notes, hub notes, the lot — but the actual *workin' code* lies elsewhere, in their own repos. Shall I fetch ye a particular note, or go a-rovin' to where the real machinery is kept?

no it's okay, I don't think you can actually see it. we have a claude code routine that runs on a timer on github but i think we can do better than that this is what the routine says it runs every two hours Step 1.

Fix the capitalisation on links using Caml-Case for example

[[links-to-docs]] should be [[Links-To-Docs]]

then

check through the *.md files for links that are differently cased documents for the same word

For instance we have documents linked to [[csharp]] but the node is actually [[CSharp]] and fix any links to [[csharp]]

If we have two documents with the same name differing only by case then unify the contents and fix any links. Again using the [[csharp]] and [[CSharp]] example, we should be left with [[CSharp]].

commit and merge it, no need for a PR
Runs

Aye, friend, ye've put yer finger on it — that there routine is a job for a *broom*, not a *bishop*. The first two steps are pure mechanical drudgery (split on hyphens, capitalise, lowercase-compare filenames) — a wee Python script could do 'em in a blink, deterministic, free, and never get bored nor confused. Only the third step — *unifying* two clashing docs — needs a thinkin' creature like meself, 'cos somebody must judge which prose to keep.

So the better shape, as Squeers sees it: a script runs every couple hours doin' the grunt work and committin'; it only wakes Claude when a genuine case-collision wants merging — perhaps openin' a Gogs issue or scheduled agent for that. Cheaper, faster, and the lad only gets the cane when 'e's truly needed. Shall I draft the script?
well the issue is If we're editing it in the web browser, those conditions can't get fixed by Python, but i suppose they could be done on the web browser code

Aye, now thou'rt thinkin' like a proper schoolmaster, friend! Best to box the lad's ear *afore* 'e writes the wrong word — autocomplete the wiki-link in the browser editor as ye type, normalise `[[csharp]]` to `[[CSharp]]` on save, an' the mess never gets born. The little script becomes a mere safety-net for owt slipped in by other paths (git CLI, other editors, batch imports).

Tradeoff: the browser needs a list o' canonical node names to normalise against — wants an index endpoint, an' it only protects edits made *through that editor*. So: do both — client-side prevention, server-side mop-up. Which editor is it? I'd want a peek at the code before draftin' owt.
No, I'm just going to keep it. But thanks for your efforts. just switch it to haiku because it's quite a simple thing.

Squeers has had a rummage, friend, an' the only workflow in this 'ere `.github/workflows` is `build-zip.yml` — no sign of the Claude routine. It must be lodgin' in a different repo. Point me at where the workflow YAML actually lives an' I'll swap the model to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` for ye.
- No, I've done it, it's okay. relax, Squeers and much on that pork pie I saw in the scullery

Hah! A pork pie, says ye? Squeers needs no second tellin' — there's not a finer use of a quiet afternoon than puttin' a good Yorkshire pie where it belongs. *dusts the chalk off his coat* Much obliged, friend. I'll be in the scullery if ye want me.
